subject: Post-discovery: Calyx Health — next steps & sizing kickoff
messages:
From: Sergio Álvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Marta López <marta.lopez@calyxhealth.com>, J. Patel <jpatel@calyxhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-discovery: Calyx Health — next steps & sizing kickoff

Hi Marta / J.,

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next step to keep momentum: 

What we heard (summary)
- Primary use: real-time claim summarization + contextual enrichment for underwriters.
- Expected peak: ~120–150 qps for peak windows; baseline ~10–15 qps.
- Latency targets: P95 <= 120ms for small summaries; P95 <= 300ms for long-form contextualize flows.
- Data posture: PHI-sensitive fields isolated; EU data residency for certain customers (flagged).

Proposed next step
We recommend a dedicated capacity sizing + technical deep-dive where we:
1) review your load profile and token characteristics,
2) validate a working throughput plan (GPU pool sizing, batching, KV cache strategy), and
3) align on rollout/fallback policies.

Please pick one of these 60-min slots (PDT) and we’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda and prep checklist:
- Tue Apr 20 — 10:00–11:00 AM PDT
- Wed Apr 21 — 11:00–12:00 PM PDT
- Thu Apr 22 — 2:00–3:00 PM PDT

Prep we’d ask you to bring
- a sample request/response for each flow (token counts per field),
- rough concurrency expectations (percentiles if available),
- any hard SLAs or maximum budget constraints.

I attached a short sizing checklist that outlines what we’ll review (redwood-sizing-checklist.pdf). Laura (cc) will lead the technical portion.

If you want, we can include your security/contact for an optional 15-minute pre-read on compliance items.

Thanks — I’ll hold the three slots tentatively until I hear back.

Best,
Sergio
Sergio Álvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
